title: Server side sessions with rotation and expiry
when: Login works in a Node app and now real session management is needed: storage, idle and absolute expiry, rotation on login and privilege change, logout of one or all devices.
prompt:
Goal: sessions.mjs that creates, looks up, rotates and revokes sessions, storing only a hash of each session id.
Steps:
1. create(userId): id = randomBytes(32).toString("base64url"); save under sha256(id) with { userId, createdAt, lastSeen, userAgent }; return the raw id for the cookie only.
2. lookup(id): hash, load, reject when idle over 30 minutes or older than 7 days; refresh lastSeen at most once a minute.
3. rotate(oldId): new id, same data, old row deleted; call it on login, password change and role increase.
4. revoke(id) on logout; revokeAll(userId) after password reset and for a "log out other devices" button.
5. Cookie: sid=<id>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age equal to the absolute limit; clear with Max-Age=0.
6. Delete expired rows from an unref timer every 10 minutes.
Quality bar:
- A leaked database dump holds no usable session ids.
- Session rows hold ids and flags, never passwords or tokens.
- Each lookup is one keyed read.
Pitfalls:
- Keeping the pre login id after login (session fixation).
- Sliding expiry with no absolute cap.
- Memory only sessions that silently log everyone out on restart.
Verify:
- [ ] The stored key is a hash.
- [ ] Idle and absolute expiry both have tests.
- [ ] Login and password change rotate the id.
- [ ] revokeAll ends other devices.
Output: sessions.mjs, cookie helpers in auth.mjs, test/sessions.test.mjs.

examples.input: adicionar sair de todos os dispositivos e expirar sessao inativa
examples.output: hashed session ids, 30 min idle and 7 day cap, rotate on login, revokeAll(userId)
